questions.q: In the post office picture, Kafka is the post office. What is Kafka Connect?
options: A second post office next door
The mail that gets sent
The delivery service carrying parcels between the post office and other buildings
The stamp that proves a parcel arrived
questions.explain: Kafka Connect moves data between Kafka and other systems. A source connector brings data in, and a sink connector sends it out.

questions.q: Your database changes all day. Does Kafka Connect notice each insert, update and delete by itself?
options: Yes, every connector does it
Yes, but only on a paid plan
Only if you switch on a special setting
No, a CDC connector such as Debezium does that part
questions.explain: Kafka Connect only supplies the frame that runs a CDC connector. Debezium is one such connector set.

questions.q: You want the job to keep going if one machine dies. Which mode fits?
options: Distributed, because the work is shared across many workers
Standalone, because one process is simpler to keep alive
Either one, they behave the same
Neither, Kafka Connect can't survive a failure
questions.explain: Standalone runs in one process and has no fault tolerance. Distributed spreads the work, so it's the one to use in production.

questions.q: A job is copying records and hits one bad one. What happens by default?
options: The bad record is skipped quietly
The job stops, because it fails fast
The bad record goes to a side shelf for later
The job waits an hour and tries again
questions.explain: By default Kafka Connect stops at the first error. You can change that, but it's good to know before your first surprise.

questions.q: Stretch question. The post warns about the web interface used to control Kafka Connect. What is the warning?
options: It is locked to administrators until you unlock it
It is switched off unless you ask for it
It can only look at jobs, never change them
It is open by default, so anyone who can reach it can start and stop jobs
questions.explain: By default the REST API is unsecured, so share access only with people you trust. Yes, really.
